clue.text: Caption can say in advance

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, so the short example word goes into the middle of the verb

blocks.note: to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a caption can predict what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say in advance' looks like one phrase meaning predict, but 'say' and 'advance' are separate pieces, and 'in' puts one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The explanatory text printed beneath a picture or map is called its legend.

clue.text: Former lover cuddles regularly just for show

indicators.note: taking letters at a steady interval means keeping every second one of the word

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An old flame embraces someone only to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just for show' reads as one phrase about insincerity; only 'show' is the definition, as in a face that shows or exudes confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude a quality is to display it plainly, so it is a verb close to show or radiate.

clue.text: Parks cars in residential areas

blocks.note: first meaning: large landed grounds around country houses

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their vehicles on the streets where people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parks' looks like a verb about leaving cars; it is a noun. 'Cars' adds a third sense: an estate car is a British station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Country estates are private parkland, and housing estates are planned districts of homes, so one plural noun covers both.

clue.text: After leaving college, messy bed could go for a bomb

indicators.note: once something has left, it is no longer present, so that letter is taken away
a messy arrangement is jumbled, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A student leaves university, and their untidy bed is so bad it might as well be bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the C out of 'bed could go' and shuffle what is left. A doodlebug was the British nickname for the V-1 flying bomb of 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the wartime British slang name for the German V-1 flying bomb, a pilotless missile.

clue.text: They treat poorly young lady, a drug addict that's been admitted

indicators.note: someone admitted has been let inside, so this word goes within the other

blocks.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
a user is someone who takes drugs

explanation.surface: A young woman with a drug habit has been taken into hospital and is badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' suggests a hospital, but it is the signal to put one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Misusers handle things wrongly or abuse them, so they are people who treat something badly.

clue.text: Show with numbers: fifty one plus one hundred and one add up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A piece of arithmetic: totting up fifty-one, a hundred and one.
explanation.walkthrough: LACISUM is built, then read upwards. 'Numbers' is the trap: here it means songs, not figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show whose story is carried by songs, which theatre people call numbers.

clue.text: Rock and roll single not selling without sleeve

indicators.note: a record taken out of its sleeve has its covering stripped, so the outer parts of these words go
something that rolls over turns round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the end of single, the word not and the start of selling

explanation.surface: A rock and roll record that is failing in the shops is being sold without its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll single' reads as one music phrase; 'Rock' is the definition, and 'roll' turns the hidden letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone is the hard mineral material of rock, and a stone is a small piece of rock.

clue.text: Lied, say, with boy about drug, causing a fuss

blocks.note: a Lied is a German art song; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A boy lied about drugs and caused trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lied' looks like the past of lie; it is the German word for song (plural Lieder).
explanation.definitionFit: Making a song and dance about something is an idiom for an unnecessary fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Mo Farah, for example, has drink with those he beat

blocks.note: Mo Farah is a British Olympic distance runner

explanation.surface: The champion athlete shares a drink with the rivals he defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up are the competitors who finish behind the winner, so they are those a champion beats.

clue.text: They have lots of empty cans after getting gold can-opener!

indicators.note: the opener of a word is whatever starts it, so only its initial letter is kept
read as made of, the tins are built around the nothing that fills them

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an empty quantity is nothing, zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tramp's can-opener turns out to be gold, and leaves a heap of empty tins behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags a loose construction: empty cans are tins holding nothing, so a zero sits inside them. 'Lots' are items for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctions sell goods in numbered lots, so they are things that have lots.

clue.text: Having gown in for slight alteration

indicators.note: a garment sent for alteration gets remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has a dress taken in at the dressmaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' looks like the start of a sentence about a dress fitting; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something means possessing it, which is what having it means.

clue.text: Sick, mostly after having fast pulse

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after fasting, and their pulse is quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast pulse' looks like a racing heart, but 'pulse' means an edible seed of the bean family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the dried edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one of the commonest.

clue.text: Detective is with a luxury car that's flipped over and burnt

indicators.note: something flipped over is upside down, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A detective at the scene of a crash where a posh car has overturned and burnt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremated means reduced to ashes by fire, as a body is at a crematorium.

clue.text: They increase the power of current measures

blocks.note: second meaning: units of electric current

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current measures' sounds like present-day policies; it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Amps is short both for amplifiers, which boost a signal, and for amperes, the units of electric current.

clue.text: Shows bottom and head in scene shown on satellite

blocks.note: to moon is to bare one's bottom

explanation.surface: Someone bares their backside on a broadcast beamed via satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite' suggests satellite TV; here it is the Moon itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonscape is the landscape of the Moon, Earth's natural satellite, as seen in photographs.

clue.text: Nonsense! This race isn't so hairy!

blocks.note: a dash is a sprint race

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim that this race is less frightening than people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' is slang for scary, so the surface sounds like a race being called less frightening; the wordplay takes it literally, as having less hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, so it is an exclamation dismissing something as nonsense.

clue.text: Relaxed with a walk in the park before working

blocks.note: a walk in the park is an idiom for something easy
a machine that is going is working

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a stroll before starting work.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going person is calm and tolerant, untroubled by things, which is to be relaxed.

clue.text: Galleons at sea arrive finally at South American city

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or adrift, so the letters are jumbled
what comes finally is at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the word's final letter, as 'finally' says

explanation.surface: Spanish galleons sail in to a South American port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American city' wants to be read together; 'South' gives S, and the definition is just 'American city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is a major city of California in the United States, so an American city.

clue.text: First person to be queen in charge? Anne's first for this land

blocks.note: the first-person form of to be, as in I am
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A historical puzzle: who first became queen, and was it Anne?
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' suggests a pioneer, but it is grammar: AM is the first-person form of the verb to be.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a country or continent, so it can stand for a land named in the clue.

clue.text: Boy, turning scarlet close to girls, runs

indicators.note: turning round means the colour word is read from the other end
the close of a word is its end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
close to means its final letter

explanation.surface: A boy blushes when near girls and runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the boy fleeing; it is a noun for the lines of unravelled stitches in tights, which British English calls ladders.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a ladder is a run in tights or stockings, so ladders are runs.

clue.text: Pauses and quietly breaks wind

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the musical letter goes within

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a moment and discreetly breaks wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps are breaks or intervals in time or speech, so as plural nouns they mean pauses.

clue.text: Walk off over pitch to have a little gander

blocks.note: to pitch is to throw, to sling

explanation.surface: Someone strolls across a sports pitch to take a quick look around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a little gander' is slang for take a quick look; here a gander is a male goose and the definition is its young.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a young goose, so a little gander in the sense of a small goose.

clue.text: Bill and Edward go round to smell cut rose

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its last letter
going round something means surrounding it, so the abbreviation wraps the other word

blocks.note: a bill or poster is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Two men walk around to sniff a freshly cut rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut rose' looks like a flower; 'cut' trims the smell word, and 'rose' is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and ascended means went up, the same tense and sense.

clue.text: See 7
Scandalmonger turns to drink

blocks.note: goes, as in turns in a game; the clue spells the plural gos

explanation.surface: A rumour-spreader takes to the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is a person who spreads rumours and tittle-tattle about others, a scandalmonger.

clue.text: The best members of Countryside Alliance

indicators.note: members belong to a body, so the letters come from within the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The finest people in a rural campaigning group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Countryside Alliance is a British lobby group for rural life and field sports.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal is the perfect example of something, the best that can be imagined.

clue.text: Country home to accommodate Old King Cole first

indicators.note: accommodating a guest means taking them in, so the letter goes inside
this says the singer's name is placed at the front of the other piece

blocks.note: Nat King Cole, the American singer

explanation.surface: A country house puts up the nursery-rhyme monarch before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Cole' is the nursery-rhyme king, but 'Old' is split off as O and King Cole points to Nat King Cole.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people with its own state and territory, so in ordinary use a country.

clue.text: Thrilled to get one pound in return for kiss that's drawn out

indicators.note: something returned comes back the other way, so these two letters are read backwards
getting one thing for another is an exchange, so a letter is swapped out

blocks.note: I is one and L is a pound
a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to receive a pound back for a kiss that lasted a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXCITED, the X is swapped for LI. 'Drawn out' sounds like prolonged, as the kiss seems, but means coaxed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out of someone, so elicited means drawn out.

clue.text: Airline after boarding puts off those who argue

indicators.note: passengers boarding go into a vehicle, so the airline letters go inside the verb

blocks.note: to deter is to put off

explanation.surface: An airline's boarding process discourages passengers who might complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Debaters argue formally for or against a motion, so they are people who argue.

clue.text: In a strong wind, horse carried a group of 20 Down

indicators.note: something carried is held within, so the horse word sits inside the weather word

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind
gee-gee, a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse is swept along in a storm with a flock of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is the collective noun for geese on the ground, and goslings grow into geese.
